text:
Maya: Heads up — after landing int8 on the new small-ranker v0.9 build we see a reproducible MRR drop ~3.5% on the short-query slice. Noticed during the nightly bakeoff. :thinking:
Alex: ugh, short queries only? what slice definition are you using here?
Maya: short = queries with <= 12 tokens after tokenization (our holdout slice). Eval harness: `eval/ndcg_mrr.py --split=short-queries --model=small-ranker-v0.9-int8`
Liam: can you confirm candidate ordering + sampling was identical to the fp16 baseline run? ordering shuffles can kill metrics.
Maya: good call — I re-ran with `--seed=42 --preserve-order` and the drop persists. Baseline fp16 run from last week: MRR 0.456, int8 run: 0.441
Rahul: any changes to tokenizer or prompt formatting between builds? even subtle whitespace can shift short queries.
Maya: tokenizer code unchanged. But the model artifact differs (q4_0 -> q8_0 path and then int8 conversion step).
Emily: have you checked kv cache handling / prefix caching? small models sometimes treat past_key_values differently post-quant.
Maya: KV cache looked fine in basic smoke. No OOMs, but I'll add a targeted trace.
ops-bot: CI:rerank-bakeoff started for 1711001234 — logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/1711001234
Alex: can we reproduce on a tiny synthetic dataset where we can inspect top-k logits? If logits are compressed weirdly we'll see softmax shifts.
Maya: creating a tiny 200-query probe now. Will push results in ~15m.
Liam: also test with query padding to 32 tokens vs dynamic. We saw earlier that padding changes relative positions for short queries with quantized kernels.
Maya: ran probe: int8 scores skew slightly higher for second-ranked candidate causing tie-break shifts. I can paste a small example:
Maya: ```
# example doc scores for query Q123
baseline_fp16: [1.23, 0.97, 0.54]
int8:         [1.21, 1.00, 0.52]
# ranking changes: candidate 2 jumps over 1 for ~12% of probe queries
```
Rahul: that looks like a calibration/scale issue rather than full semantic loss. Maybe embedding or final-head scaling got quantized differently.
Emily: do we have per-layer quant stats? histograms for last linear before softmax?
Maya: not yet, will dump activations for the final head on the probe set.
Alex: as mitigation options: 1) try hybrid quant (keep final head in fp16), 2) per-channel scaling re-estimation, 3) temperature calibration post-quant.
Liam: try hybrid first — minimal runtime hit and often fixes ranking. Also run eval with deterministic topk tie-break to measure worst-case.
Maya: starting hybrid run (keep last linear fp16) and a safety run with `--pad-to=32`. Posting results when done.
ops-bot: CI:hybrid-1711001234 queued on dedicated-gpu-pool-3
Maya: quick update — hybrid run MRR = 0.453 (almost recovered), pad-to-32 + hybrid = 0.455. Looks promising.
Rahul: nice. That suggests quantization noise concentrated in final head / short-query scoring sensitivity.
Emily: we should add a unit-level regression test for short-query slice in the eval gauntlet and a check that hybrid fallback is enabled in the release config for now.
Alex: agree. Also log a postmortem entry and schedule a small experiment to re-calibrate per-channel scales during conversion instead of naive round-to-nearest.
Maya: will open PR with: 1) hybrid quant conversion script, 2) pad-to-32 as optional preproc knob, 3) new short-query holdout test in nightly gauntlet.
Liam: add a note in model catalog that v0.9-int8 has known ~MRR short-query sensitivity and that dedicated instances use hybrid by default until we retrain conversion.
Maya: filing follow-ups — https://tracker/redwood/ML-732 (will link conversion artifacts and CI logs). Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Alex: great triage, :rocket:
